{{Short description|78th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = National Hurling League 2009 |image =[[File:2009 National Hurling League Finals Programme.JPG|250px]] |dates =7 February 2009 – 3 May 2009 |teams = 34 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles =14th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two = Offaly |threea = Kildare |threeb = London |four = Sligo |previous =[[2008 National Hurling League|2008]] |next =[[2010 National Hurling League|2010]] }} The '''2009 National Hurling League''' (known as the '''[[Allianz]] National Hurling League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 78th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Structure== The National Hurling League saw a major restructuring of the usual four divisions with the teams divided more equitably into a five-tier structure. Division 1 was a single division and was confined to the top eight teams. The top two teams in the division qualified for the final. Division 2 operated in a similar manner. Division 3A was a newly created division and consisted of six teams. The top two teams in the division qualified for the final. Division 3B operated in a similar manner, however, that division consisted of seven teams. Division 4 was a single division consisting of six teams. On 3 May 2009, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after a 4–17 to 2-26 extra-time win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. It was their first league title since 2006 and their 14th National League title overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hogan-goes-extra-yard-of-plucky-tipperary-26533407.html|title=Hogan goes extra yard of plucky Tipperary|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 May 2009|access-date=19 February 2016}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-kilkenny-v-tipperary-2009-allianz-hurling-league-final/|title =Flashback: 2009 Allianz Hurling League Final - Kilkenny v Tipperary|date=15 May 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=18 May 2020}} [[Clare GAA|Clare]] failed to win a single group stage game - finishing in the bottom position - and were relegated to Division 2 for the [[2010 National Hurling League|2010 league]]. Dublin's [[Alan McCrabbe]] was the Division 1 top scorer with 1-50. ===Structure=== A total of 8 teams contested the top division of the league, including all of the sides from the 2008 season that formerly took part in Divisions 1A and 1B. Due to the restructuring the 2008 Division 2 champions did not gain promotion to the top tier. Each team played all the others in its group once, earning 2 points for a win and 1 for a draw.
